requirement:
When loading a supported legacy evidence record that did not capture its
procedure version, Habeas Codicem represents that missing version as `*`.
In-place conversion preserves this wildcard rather than assigning the current
version. The wildcard matches any
requested review revision under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records.procedure_match`.
The record is current when its recorded inputs and all existing application
freshness checks still match. Version matching leaves the subject, reference-set,
input, determination, citation, and site checks intact.

For new assessments, Habeas Codicem's validation value supplies a concrete review revision
other than `*`, and the assessment records it.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_conversion.legacy_freshness`. I judged this from the supplied test source and did not request any implementation source.

- **Missing version is loaded as `*`.**
  - `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[legacy_conversion_preserves_every_historical_field_without_resolving_sources]` decodes legacy records for a definition, a citation and a site. It asserts `record.revision == "*"` and that the output and dependencies are preserved.
  - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once]` loads legacy records for every review kind and asserts `loaded.revision == "*"`.
- **In-place conversion keeps the wildcard.**
  - The same `evidence_format.rs` test asserts that `encode` writes `review_version == "*"`, and that `view(native)` round-trips to the old record.
  - `src/authoring/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[current_legacy_authoring_converts_without_configuration_and_stdout_never_converts]` runs the real authoring conversion on a file. It asserts the rewritten file has `review_version == "*"` and still views as the old record, and that stdout output does not convert.
- **The wildcard matches any requested revision.**
  - `src/evidence_format.rs#mod[tests]/fn[native_freshness_checks_versions_inputs_and_application_fields]` calls `record_is_current` with `"future-review-version"` on a `*` record and gets true.
  - The same test shows that a different concrete stored version does not match `REVIEW_VERSION`.
  - It also shows that a changed input makes a `*` record stale even for the requested revision `"any"`.
- **Current means inputs and application checks still match.**
  - The legacy tests assert that unmodified legacy records produce no findings from `inspect_repository`.
  - The native `*` and concrete forms give identical findings, and loading does not modify the file.
- **Version matching leaves the other checks intact.** `every_review_kind_loads_both_formats_and_reports_each_application_failure_once` applies one mutation at a time to `*` records. Each must produce the expected finding, and the legacy and converted forms must produce the same findings. The mutations are:
  - Determination changes (`determination` set to false).
  - A changed input hash or text.
  - Changed subject text and a changed reference-set hash for definitions.
  - A changed file, item or commentary for citations.
  - A changed requirement, file, item, queries, fixmes or `applies` for sites.
- **New assessments use a concrete revision.** `authoring_keeps_the_prepared_subject_snapshot_and_concrete_version` asserts that the produced value's `review_version` equals `REVIEW_VERSION` and is not `"*"`. It also decodes the record and checks that its dependencies are recorded. That test uses a single requirement subject, but the text does not distinguish new assessments by subject kind.

I found no uncovered obligation and no wrong expected result. There are no acknowledgments, and none are needed.

// Defined in habeas_sdk::graph.
/// Compare the saved review-rule revision with the currently requested revision.
pub fn procedure_matches(stored: &str, requested: &str) -> bool;
The revision matches when the stored `Record::revision` is `*` or equals the
requested revision exactly. Only the complete stored value `*` is a wildcard;
other values compare literally. A wildcard leaves dependency comparison and
result decoding unchanged. It matches revisions for the selected source and
criterion only, and does not supply evidence for other criteria.
